premise: At 54 I drained my late husband’s $210,000 life insurance to buy a shuttered 1930s movie palace with my son, who signed a partnership giving me 49% equity; once he lined up a $1.5‑million development deal he forged a gift deed, bulldozed the theater, and handed me a $2,000 ‘relocation’ check. I found our original contract in a safe‑deposit box, proved the forgery, and won a $680,000 fraud judgment plus the vacant lot—I built an outdoor revenge drive‑in called ‘Projectionist’s Revenge,’ and my son is court‑ordered to run the snack bar in a vintage usher uniform while a short documentary about his perjury plays before every movie.
